Question: What is the role of the Internship & Skills Development Unit?
Reference answer:
The Internship & Skills Development Unit was established in the Faculty of Humanities of
the University of Kelaniya in 2019 in order to to assist student who pursue their degree in
the Arts stream to overcome the complex challenges they will have to face as graduates
after their study period. The establishment of this unit was based on a concept of the
AHEAD project, which was implemented with assistance from World Bank. The primary
aim of setting up this academic unit was to increase the student’s employability and to
develop the associated skills, thus playing a unique role in the Faculty of Humanities. The
unit’s objectives are as follows:
• Directing the students for authentic industrial training related to employment within and
without the subject field they are studying within the period of studying the degree.
• Providing opportunities for students to engage with public and private sector
institutions in Sri Lanka to gain professional competence in matters such as corporate
administrative structures and management, the operation of corporate rules and ethics,
and the nature of a work environment.
• Expanding services and opportunities to help develop a student’s personality for
employment.
• To develop in the students the ability to manage the three languages of Sinhala, English
and Tamil for office work.
• To improve the use of information technology and to develop computer literacy in
students which is a special need concerning professional competencies today.
• To develop leadership qualities in the students and to promote their teamwork skills,
decision-making skills, organizational skills, and ability to perform any task well
• To develop the ability to work in a manner that respects others and does not violate
the rights of others in the Sri Lankan society that comprises different languages,
cultures and lifestyles.
• To develop the ability to adapt to any work environment and to build a sense of
responsibility and accountability in the students.
• In addition to the subject knowledge, developing application and presentation skills
that should exist in the students, as well as developing the basic statistical and
analytical knowledge essential in office work.
To achieve the above objectives, so far the Internship & Skills Development Unit has
introduced about 08 career-oriented subject units covering 12 credits. Being allowed to
complete these subject units as an essential part of the degree course can also be said to be
a privilege for you as a student to add a new value to your degree certificates.
Author: Aysha

Question: What is a fall-back qualification, and how can a student become eligible for it?
Reference answer: A fall-back qualification is an alternative qualification awarded to students who are unable to fulfill the requirements of their intended degree within the maximum period allowed. A student who fails to meet the requirements for a BSc (General) degree after six academic years may apply for a Higher Diploma in Science (SLQF Level 4) or a Diploma in Science (SLQF Level 3). A student who fails to meet the requirements for a BSc Honours degree after seven academic years may apply for a Bachelor of Science General Degree (SLQF Level 5). The Faculty Board of Science must recommend the award after conducting an exit interview and obtaining Senate approval. Students expelled on disciplinary grounds may not be eligible for a fall-back qualification.
Supporting passage(s):
A student who fails to fulfil the above requirements in section 4.5.1 for BSc
(General) degree, after completing maximum period of six academic years
allowed for the degree become eligible to apply for fall-back qualification of a
Higher Diploma in Science (SLQF Level 4) or Diploma in Science (SLQF Level
3). Moreover, a student who fails to fulfil the requirements in section 4.5.2 for
BSc Honours degree, after completing maximum period of seven academic years
allowed for the degree become eligible to apply for fall-back qualification of a
Bachelor of Science General Degree (SLQF Level 5). However, a student expelled
from the university on disciplinary grounds, might not be eligible for fall-back
qualification.
A recommendation for award of a fall-back qualification to a student who
applied for Bachelor of Science or Higher Diploma in Science or Diploma in
Science under above condition should be made by the Faculty Board of Science,
to the Senate, after an exit interview to judge the suitability of the student to the
applied qualifications.
The effective date of award of a fall-back qualification of Bachelor of Science or
Higher Diploma in Science or Diploma in Science will be the first day the month
after which the Senate has approved the award of the qualification.

Question: What are the eligibility requirements to sit for examinations?
Reference answer:
Have at least 80% attendance for both theory and practical sessions.
Satisfy all course requirements set by the relevant teacher.
Submit valid medical/official approval documents if absent for accepted reasons.
Supporting passage(s):
I. Attendance for Lectures
One hundred percent regular attendance is expected from each student. A student who does not
have 80% attendance for both theory and practical and has not satisfied the course requirements
maintained by the teacher concern shall not be eligible to sit for the end-semester examination
and given IC (Incomplete) symbol whereas the candidate shall be required to repeat the course
in the subsequent semester. The candidate shall be awarded maximum of a “C” grade which is
equivalent to GP 2.00 for that paper/course.

Students are requested to obtain prior approval from the Dean of the Faculty by submitting a
letter of request issued by the Director/ Physical Education to support the absence from course
work due to any kind of sports activities inside the University system. Representatives of the
Students’ Union must submit official document(s) to the Dean of the Faculty to support the
absence from course work due to official Union Meetings/activities.

II. Submission of Medical Report
Students who fail to continue course work due to medical reasons are requested to submit a
proper medical certificate issued by the government hospitals/Registered Medical
Practitioners/University Medical Officer (UMO).
Under exceptional circumstances certificates issued by other sources could be validated by
University Medical Board (UMB). A medical certificate may be obtained from the following
authorities.
• University Medical Officer (UMO)
• District Medical Officer (DMO)
• Consultant specialist in the relevant field
• Head of the Government Base Hospital
• Medical Superintendent of an Ayurveda / Government Hospital
• Ayurveda Physician registered in Ayurveda Medical Council

III. Repeat Examination

• If a candidate obtains below C pass or GP <2.00 in a paper, she/he must repeat the
paper.
• Those who failed in a course unit are required to sit for the said examination when it is
held next.
• A candidate can repeat a paper not more than thrice. A grace chance may be considered
with the approval of the Faculty Board of Arts and Culture and the subsequent Senate,
EUSL.
• A repeat candidate shall be awarded a maximum C grade/GP 2.00 in the respective
paper.

IV. Absence from the Examination
Except for any justifiable reasons to the Faculty Board and the Medical grounds supported by
a valid medical certificate, she/he is considered as absent. A student who has failed in a
particular course has to repeat the course at the first available opportunity. The maximum grade
given for a repeated examination shall be C or GP of 2.00

A student who falls sick during examination should contact the UMO immediately. While a
student falls sick at home or elsewhere during the examination time student’s parents/guardian
should inform the Dean of the Faculty of Arts & Culture within seven (07) days by telegram
followed by a letter. The medical certificate also should be sent to the Dean of the Faculty of
Arts & culture within fourteen (14) days.

If a Bachelor Degree or Honours Degree student has completed a period of six (06) and eight
(08) academic years respectively from the date of Registration at the EUSL, the registration of
the student shall lapse after the above-said stipulated period.
